Interface GamePhaseBehavior

All Superinterfaces:
Serializable
All Known Implementing Classes:
ChangeAgePhase, EndGamePhase, EndTurnPhase, PlayerTurnPhase, SetupPhase, StartTurnPhase, TurnPhase
public interface GamePhaseBehavior extends Serializable
Represents the behavior of a specific game phase within the State design pattern.

This interface defines the set of actions that can be performed during any game phase. Each concrete implementation of this interface will provide the logic for a specific phase (e.g., SetupPhase, PlayerTurnPhase).

By default, all methods emit a GameEvent.Type.INVALID_PHASE event and throw IllegalMoveException. Concrete states must override the methods corresponding to the actions allowed in that phase. This ensures that an action invoked in an incorrect phase results in a clear error.

    • handlePlayerDisconnect

      default boolean handlePlayerDisconnect(GameState context, Player player)
      Reacts to a player disconnecting while this phase is active.

      The player has already been marked disconnected on the model when this is called. The default implementation does nothing: most phases have no notion of a "current" player whose turn must be skipped (they are transient or do not await a specific player's input). Only the phases that actively wait for a single player — StartTurnPhase (tile occupation) and PlayerTurnPhase (card/building drafting) — override this to advance past the player who left. This is a lifecycle hook, not a player action, so it never throws IllegalMoveException.

      Parameters:
      context - the GameState context for the state pattern
      player - the player who just disconnected
      Returns:
      true if this phase advanced as a result, false otherwise

    • resolveActivePlayer

      default Optional<Player> resolveActivePlayer(GameState context)
      Resolves the player this phase is currently awaiting an action from.

      This is the authoritative source for "whose turn it is" in the public snapshot, replacing index-based lookups (e.g. turnOrder.get(index)) that break when a disconnected player occupies an earlier tile: such lookups count connected and disconnected occupiers inconsistently and end up pointing at the wrong player. The default returns Optional.empty() — most phases are transient or await no specific player. PlayerTurnPhase and StartTurnPhase override this with their own active player.

      Parameters:
      context - the GameState context for the state pattern
      Returns:
      the player currently expected to act, or empty if none
